rule.docs:
# empty-comment (PLR2044)

Derived from the **Pylint** linter.

Fix is always available.

## What it does
Checks for a # symbol appearing on a line not followed by an actual comment.

## Why is this bad?
Empty comments don't provide any clarity to the code, and just add clutter.
Either add a comment or delete the empty comment.

## Example
```python
class Foo:  #
    pass
```

Use instead:
```python
class Foo:
    pass
```

## References
- [Pylint documentation](https://pylint.pycqa.org/en/latest/user_guide/messages/refactor/empty-comment.html)

analysis.summary: Flags lines ending with a '#' character without following non-whitespace text.
analysis.fixDescription: Removes the trailing '#' and any whitespace immediately preceding it on the same line, leaving the rest of the line unchanged.
hazards: If the '#' is part of a string literal (e.g., `s = "abc#"  #`), removing it alters the string value.
If the '#' is inside a byte string or f-string (e.g., `b"data#"  #` or `f"{x}#"  #`), the fix corrupts the literal content.
If the line contains a backslash continuation before the '#' (e.g., `x = 1 \  #`), removing the '#' may break the continuation if whitespace handling changes.
If the '#' appears in a decorator (e.g., `@decorator#  #`), the fix could produce invalid syntax by merging tokens.
If the '#' is in a type annotation comment (e.g., `x = 1  # type: int  #`), the fix removes only the last '#', potentially leaving a malformed type comment.
If the '#' is followed by a newline in a multi-line statement via implicit line joining (e.g., within parentheses), the fix may affect where the line breaks are interpreted.
If the '#' is the only content on a line used to disable a linter directive via `# noqa` but written as `#  #`, the fix removes both, disabling the intent.
If the '#' is part of an emoji or non-ASCII symbol in a comment-like context (e.g., `x = 1  #😀  #`), the fix may leave invalid or confusing remnants.
If the line is otherwise blank except for indentation and `#` (e.g., `    #`), the fix removes the '#' and may leave only whitespace, which could be insignificant but alters formatting.
If the '#' is in a line that also contains a semicolon statement separator (e.g., `x=1; y=2  #`), the fix does not affect semantics but may mislead if the '#' was intended to start a comment.

results.title: File Modes and Truncation - Partial Write Hazard
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment affecting file mode logic; after fix, incorrect file mode opens file in 'w' instead of 'a', causing truncation.

results.title: Dict Ordering and Duplicate Keys - Hash Collision After Rewrite
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment on dict key assignment; key expression changes from variable to literal due to whitespace removal, altering hash and causing duplicate key collision in dict cons

results.title: Byte String and F-string Literal Corruption
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment on line with f-string containing '#'; fix deletes the '#' from the f-string literal itself, changing runtime value.

-s2 = b"data#"  #

 print(s2)
 # Recovery: reset and show correct behavior

results.title: Type Annotations Evaluated at Runtime
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment on line with forward reference in type annotation; fix breaks annotation resolution causing NameError at runtime when annotation is evaluated.

results.title: Emoji and Non-ASCII in Comment Context
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' and preceding whitespace from line with emoji in comment; after fix, emoji becomes adjacent to code or corrupted due to incorrect whitespace removal, changing interpretation.

findings.detail: model expected the rule to fire, it stayed silent

results.title: Star-Imports and Module-Level Side Effects
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment on line with star-import; fix alters import statement by removing critical whitespace, causing __all__ to be misinterpreted or import to fail.

results.title: Truthiness of Custom __bool__ and None vs Falsy
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment on line assigning object with custom __bool__; fix alters line to remove whitespace causing unintended tuple creation, changing truthiness evaluation.

results.title: Mutable Default Arguments and Aliasing After Rewrite
results.hazard: Rule removes trailing '#' from comment on function definition with mutable default argument; fix alters indentation or line structure causing default argument to be re-evaluated or shared incorrectly
